scope: Local code, owned disposable PostgreSQL and synthetic HTTP only. No production/staging operation or backup changes. No additional migration, pool/concurrency limit change or new infrastructure.
changes: Read group/review parents with the original predicates/order; conditionally read children only for actual parent IDs. Empty groups and confirmed days skip two empty child SELECTs in the standalone fixture.

Verified GET/HEAD calculations share one bounded monthly snapshot by transactional revision, project visibility/channel and import. Cost and point consumers reuse the same canonical calculation; optional ignored-name metadata is projected afterwards.

V8 serialization stays entirely inside process memory, preserving Date, Map, number precision and internal aliases, with an independent graph for each consumer. Eight entries/8 MiB total, two MiB per entry and at most 15 seconds; uses the existing opt-in flag.

Unverified callers, jobs and writes bypass monthly sharing, including writes nested in a verified read context. Source errors and decode failures are evicted; changed revisions cannot reuse old or pending results.

Progress digests canonicalize JSON object keys and explicitly unordered realized-service collections. Planned/manual/nested measurement arrays retain their order. Only digest inputs are sorted; calculation inputs are not changed. The opaque token intentionally changes algorithm once.

Each unordered realized row is encoded once and the canonical root assembled from those encodings. A pure CPU diagnostic confirmed 54 equal digests to the preceding double-encoding implementation and about 30% less digest CPU.
Binary decoding receives a copy of the serialized bytes, so typed-array views cannot expose or mutate the cache storage.

regression.method: Pre-fix diagnostic: a Node loader captured the old hash inputs in independent reader processes on identical synthetic PostgreSQL rows. Only counts/equality flags/hashes retained; source calculations were not reordered.

parity.method: Eight normalized business outputs in seven real PostgreSQL states, read in separate source processes on identical rows: explicit/latest rates, point metadata, individual/group/viewer details, confirmed days and monthly allocation report. Object keys canonicalized; Map/Set entries and all meaningful arrays preserved. Only the three top-level opaque progressRevision tokens and the monthly report generation timestamp are normalized because their algorithm/runtime time intentionally differ. All financial fields remain in the comparison.

method.http: Four sequential final-source cohorts: control/candidate then candidate/control. Both sources explicitly enable the same read-cache flag; reference is 1c26fa28, which already contains projected DTO caching. Each cohort has 832 measured 200 responses, 800 warm (100 per route/profile), eight first-process, eight warmups and sixteen after-worker-write. Eight expected authentication/module negatives separately. Final total: 3328 measured successes.
method.service: Five paired full-result service comparisons per mode/case against the original plan baseline, alternating order: 30 exact result pairs. No verified request context: the monthly snapshot is bypassed. Imports/process boot excluded, database pages warm; after-session is a SELECT rather than full HTTP authentication.
method.environment: PostgreSQL 16, one CPU/768 MiB; API pool eight, concurrency four; report-count parameter 1200 (actual counts in fixture), 297 scope lines, distributed two-member group, point summary, two profiles/two sessions each. No task tests or other database work during final timed cohorts. API host not isolated. No proxy/TLS/browser/production load measured.

cohorts.name: control-initial
cohorts.method: Synthetic loopback HTTP against the real Express app and migrated PostgreSQL. Authentication validates persisted hashed sessions through requireAuth; password login is not exercised. First-process samples use a fresh API process per request, with warm database pages and process imports excluded. Warm requests mix surfaces, profiles and two sessions per profile under a bounded shared concurrency. Client timing includes response-body receipt; server timing includes authentication and serialization. Active-pool interval samples are observations, not individual query wait times. No Nginx, TLS, browser rendering, external API or production load is measured.

sparse.method: Local paired uncached service calculations on PostgreSQL with warm database pages; not HTTP latency. Timings exclude process boot and module imports. Fresh Node/Prisma processes for every cold sample. After-session performs a SELECT, not HTTP authentication. Prisma operation profiles include mapping; sqlQueries capture pg pool calls and replay SELECTs with EXPLAIN ANALYZE after the calculation. Pool call durations overlap and include queue/event-loop delays. Initialization diagnostics run in separate processes and do not warm timed samples. Result bytes are JSON sizes, not network traffic.
sparse.cpuMethod: process.cpuUsage delta around the calculation only, before EXPLAIN replay; includes Node/Prisma CPU, excludes PostgreSQL, module imports and process boot. CPU and wall time are separate observations.

digestOptimization.method: Pure Node digest diagnostic, no database/test workload. Same actual diagnostic source rows repeated ten times; twenty warmed alternating pairs per project/division, plus first digests. Wall and whole-process CPU are separate; host not isolated. Digests equal to the preceding canonical implementation.

precedingCanonicalPrototype.decision: The first canonical version serialized realized rows twice. Retained here as exploratory evidence; the final version avoids that duplicate work while preserving the digests. These are not final-source acceptance cohorts.

limitations: The monthly snapshot is opt-in and requires an actual GET/HEAD context plus a verified transactional source revision. Its effect is separate from unconditional conditional-child reads and digest stabilization.

Only one post-write event per cohort and one cold response per route/profile: no cold/post-write p95 acceptance. Active-pool intervals have phase-dependent durations; the aggregate is not a representative 24-hour production window.
Canonical digest work adds CPU on a miss; warmed DTO reads skip that work. Four sequential cohorts do not establish causal/statistical p95 acceptance for production.
The first published read may refresh histories once due to the changed opaque digest algorithm.
Published HTTP/useful-content/LCP, two-browser UI checks, infrastructure operation over 24 hours/seven days and JobRun policy/application remain manual. Backups explicitly deferred.
